articles.title: EA is making a single-player Iron Man game
articles.summary: EA is teaming up with Marvel to make a new single-player Iron Man game. The game is currently in development at Motive Studio, which is working on the upcoming Dead Space remake.
articles.body: EA is teaming up with Marvel to make a new single-player Iron Man game, EA announced on Tuesday. The game is being developed by Motive Studio, which is working on the upcoming Dead Space remake. EA is describing this new Iron Man title as an “all-new single-player, third-person, action-adventure” Iron Man video game that will feature an “an original narrative that taps into the rich history of Iron Man, channeling the complexity, charisma, and creative genius of Tony Stark, and enabling players to feel what it’s like to truly play as Iron Man.” The new game is currently in preproduction, so it seems as if it could be quite a while before we’ll actually be able to play it. The development team is led by Olivier Proulx, who worked on Square Enix’s well-received Guardians of the Galaxy game from last year. This Iron Man title is just one of many Marvel video games currently in the works, including a currently unnamed game starring Black Panther and Captain America, the card battler Marvel Snap, and the strategy game Midnight Suns from the developers of X-COM. Disney showed glimpses of all those games and more at its recent games showcase. And in Tuesday’s blog post announcing the new Iron Man game, EA teased that it has “several new” Marvel games in development.

articles.title: Xbox’s bold plan for the future sounds nearly impossible
articles.summary: Xbox’s most recent layoffs are coupled with a goal of reaching “a billion people each day.”
articles.body: It’s another bad week for the video game industry. Microsoft outlined a series of layoffs on Monday that Xbox CEO Asha Sharma described as “the most significant restructure in Xbox history.” But buried in Sharma’s memo was a curiously optimistic statement: “I want Xbox to be one of the few companies that entertains more than a billion people each day and gives everyone the opportunity to create and connect,” she wrote. Xbox has been a shambling mess after Microsoft spent billions of dollars with little to show for it, and now it aims to reach a much bigger audience with a much smaller team, amid one of the most challenging times in the industry’s history. Sharma’s billion-person goal would sound outlandish at the best of times. Right now it sounds nearly impossible. The job cuts will see Xbox laying off 1,600 employees this summer, with another 1,600 expected over the next year. This is all part of broader restructuring at Microsoft, though the gaming division has been hit particularly hard. Four internal Xbox studios — Double Fine, Compulsion Games, Undead Labs, and Ninja Theory — are also being spun out as independent developers, which is perhaps the one bit of good news. Those studios were acquired over the years primarily to bolster the offerings on Game Pass, Microsoft’s subscription gaming service, but now it seems that the company is moving in a different direction. What is that direction? Well, it isn’t entirely clear. (Confusing strategies are pretty standard for Xbox of late.) Xbox has been losing a lot of money — Sharma claims that “in a typical year, we lost 64 cents for every dollar we invested” — and now it seems like the goal is to focus entirely on major properties that have a better chance of being blockbuster hits. Sharma says the teams that remain at Microsoft will “focus on higher priority projects.” That means not just those closely associated with the brand, like Halo and Gears of War, but also massively popular franchises under the Xbox umbrella, most notably Minecraft and Candy Crush. In fact, as part of the most recent restructuring, Helen Chiang — who previously oversaw the Minecraft franchise — has been promoted to a new role as Xbox’s chief operating officer, reporting directly to Sharma. “She will bring our businesses together under one operating model, making sure we make clear investment decisions, learn from our successes and failures, and hold ourselves accountable for results,” Sharma said of Chiang’s upgraded role. With that focus on bigger projects, some of the changes at Xbox make a certain sense. If your goal is to reach a billion people each day, a game from a quirky studio like Double Fine about a sentient lighthouse probably won’t move the needle in comparison to expanding Minecraft or Candy Crush. [Image: The Fallout TV series. But the reasoning for other cuts is much more opaque. If your goal is to lean into big games, why would you also be “making reductions” at places like Bethesda (Fallout, Elder Scrolls), id (Doom), and, perhaps Xbox’s most prolific studio, Obsidian (Avowed, The Outer Worlds)? It seems more like those teams would need further investment — and at the very least, to not have to spend the next year wondering if they’ll be hit by the next wave of layoffs — to create a major blockbuster at a time when the industry is as volatile and unpredictable as ever. You only need to look at the sorry state of the live-service space to see how poorly things can go when companies are simply chasing big numbers. The entire industry saw Fortnite become a money-printing cultural phenomenon and hoped to re-create it for themselves, collectively spending billions of dollars in the process. The result was a graveyard of canceled games and studio closures. In 2026, even Fortnite itself is struggling. This all makes Sharma’s goal of eventually reaching “a billion people each day” seem all the more absurd. It’s not clear what metric she is using to measure that number. It’s extremely unlikely Xbox will reach that in terms of daily players even if you factor in mobile games and an expansion into China and emerging markets like India, which Sharma is planning to do. King says that its lineup of games attracts more than 200 million monthly players, so you’d need quite a few Candy Crush apps to even get close. And that’s assuming that follow-ups will be as successful as the original, which is rarely the case (just ask Niantic). Sharma really wants to continue to push the Xbox brand into Hollywood, so maybe Fallout viewers — Amazon says 100 million people watched the first season — will count toward that goal. But even if you add up games, TV shows, and Game Pass subscribers, 1 billion people a day is a very large number. So instead of a clear path forward at a time of heightened uncertainty, Xbox has a vague and seemingly unattainable goal in front of it. And it’ll be doing that with a team that is smaller and will continue to shrink. “These changes are about a bigger future for Xbox,” Sharma claims, “not a smaller one.” But it’s hard to see how that’s the case. Xbox was already experiencing an identity crisis heading into these layoffs, and this lack of vision isn’t making things any clearer.

articles.title: Taylor Swift & Travis Kelce Reportedly Facing Major Marriage Challenge Amid Claims Wedding Guests Are Angry at His Behavior— ‘Very Different’
articles.summary: Sources said they used to be "pretty much inseparable."
articles.body:
Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce 's post-wedding life is about to get challenging.

According to Page Six , the couple—who tied the knot at Madison Square Garden on July 3, 2026—will be spending a lot of time apart because of their "very different" work schedules.

"Taylor and Travis spent so much time together in the months leading up to the wedding, and they were pretty much inseparable," a source told the outlet. "Now they're settling into this new rhythm as a married couple and really enjoying what that feels like."

Swift and Kelce are reportedly still "soaking up the excitement" of exchanging vows, with the insider adding, "They both still light up when they refer to each other as husband and wife, and there's something really exciting and special about that for them."

However, they have to step out of the newlywed bubble and get back to their normal lives. It seems Swift has already done so, as the source revealed she's been "pouring herself into writing new music and is incredibly inspired creatively."

"Songwriting has been her main focus, and she's really excited about what's taking shape," they added.

As for the Kansas City Chiefs tight end? He's "completely dialed in on this NFL season right now," the insider said. "He's focused on football, his team, and having the best season he possibly can."

They continued, "He's been in talks with different networks and studios over the last few years about various projects, and there are definitely opportunities there for him when the time comes, but none of that is his priority right now."

Despite their schedules looking "very different now than they did in the months leading up to the wedding," Swift and Kelce are said to be "really enjoying finding their rhythm as a married couple."

This latest update on Swift and Kelce's marriage comes just after the three-time Super Bowl champion upset a few wedding guests with his recent comments about the star-studded ceremony.

At a post-Chiefs practice press conference, Kelce reflected on his "fun offseason" before discussing his wedding. "The wedding was the best night of my life. I appreciate everybody who came out and celebrated and had fun with us," he told reporters. "It was a crazy night, and it was full of a lot of celebrations."

Kelce also shared his excitement about getting married at MSG, saying, "It's kind of cool to be able to live out my childhood dream of being in that venue, the mecca of all sports venues, to be able to get married in there."

"I can't thank the owners of MSG [enough] for allowing us to get the opportunity to do that, knowing that we wanted a private event," he noted. "It was perfect, and the AC was cooking, baby. That was the best part."

Kelce's comments reportedly struck a nerve, with some guests telling Hollywood insider Rob Shuter that they felt it was unfair that he could publicly discuss the wedding while they could not due to a strict NDA they were required to sign.

"So the bride and groom are allowed to talk about it, but we aren't?" a guest told Naughty But Nice . "It feels like there's always one rule for Taylor and another for everyone else."

Another went on to say, "Taylor and Travis can decide when to release details, photos or video because it's their wedding. But everyone else is expected to pretend they weren't even there."

Now, it's worth noting that since it was Swift and Kelce's wedding, they have every right to decide what elements get shared with the public. Fortunately for the power couple, some guests recognize and respect that choice.

"It's Taylor and Travis' wedding — of course they get to tell their own story," an insider explained. "They're the ones who got married. If they want to share memories from the night, that's their choice. The NDA was there to protect their privacy, not silence the couple."

articles.title: Hold on to your butts! This iconic “Jurassic Park” fossil just sold for $400,000 at auction
articles.summary: To whoever bought the fossilized mosquito prop: please don’t make any more dinosaurs.
articles.body:
The fossilized mosquito in amber from Jurassic Park just sold for over $400,000 at an auction.

Props from Star Trek , Harry Potter, and Superman were also sold at the Summer Entertainment Memorabilia Live Auction earlier this week.

Jurassic Park is available to stream on Hulu and Disney+.

Hold on to your butts: A major Jurassic Park movie prop was sold for an eye-popping amount of money.

The "screen-matched opening-scene" fossilized mosquito in amber from the opening scene of Jurassic Park sold for a cool $403,200, according to auction house Propstore.

"The distinctive bubbling, positioning of the embedded mosquito, and patterning where the amber meets the surrounding rock screen-match the fossil seen in close-up during the Mano de Dios mine sequence," an official description reads.

This was the first time the movie prop was offered publicly. "Few objects capture the premise and enduring cultural impact of a film so immediately, and the response from collectors reflects the significance of this remarkable piece," Propstore COO Brandon Alinger said per a press release about the sale.

It was the highest-selling item on the first day of the Summer Entertainment Memorabilia Live Auction held on Wednesday in Los Angeles.

Among other items up for bidding were the white suit John Travolta wore as Tony Manero in Saturday Night Fever , which went for $277,200, along with Christopher Reeve's Superman costume with screen- and photo-matched tunic and replica boots, selling for $233,100.

Props from Star Trek , Harry Potter , Donnie Darko , and Edward Scissorhands were also up for auction.

As fans may recall, the fossilized bug is first found in the Mano de Dios mine in the film's opening scene.

The concept of the mosquito preserved in amber reappears later in the film when Jurassic Park's excited founder John Hammond ( Richard Attenborough ) shows Dr. Grant ( Sam Neill ), Dr. Sattler ( Laura Dern ), and Dr. Malcolm ( Jeff Goldblum ) how Jurassic Park scientists have brought dinosaurs back to life.

According to Jurassic Park scientists, the insect is believed to have fed on the blood of dinosaurs millions of years ago and became fossilized after getting stuck in the sap of a tree, dino blood included.

"This fossilized tree sap, which we call amber, waited for millions of years with the mosquito inside until Jurassic Park scientists came along. Using sophisticated techniques, they extract the preserved blood from the mosquito, and, bingo! Dino DNA!"

In the final scene when those who survived the chaotic theme park escape the island, Hammond gazes longingly at his cane topped with another mosquito frozen in time by amber — another prop we would have loved.

Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter .

To whoever bought the fossilized mosquito prop: please don't make any more dinosaurs; there are several movies on why that's a bad idea.

Read the original article on Entertainment Weekly

articles.title: Fernanda Montenegro: filme do neto estreia no Festival do Rio | G1
articles.standfirst: 'Fernanda' terá sua première na 28ª edição do Festival do Rio, que acontece entre os dias 1º e 11 de outubro.
articles.summary: O documentário 'Fernanda', dirigido por Pedro Waddington, estreia no Festival do Rio celebrando os 80 anos de carreira da icônica atriz Fernanda Montenegro.
articles.body:
Fernanda Montenegro estreia documentário sobre trajetória dirigido pelo neto, Pedro Waddington. — Foto: Divulgação/Instagram/Fernanda Montenegro

A carreira da atriz Fernanda Montenegro será tema de um novo documentário dirigido por seu neto, Pedro Waddington.

Intitulado “Fernanda”, o filme fará sua première no Festival do Rio 2026, que acontece entre os dias 1º e 11 de outubro.

A produção integra a Seleção Hors Concours Première Brasil da 28ª edição do tradicional festival de cinema.

O documentário percorre diferentes momentos da vida e da carreira da atriz de 96 anos, que soma mais de oito décadas de trajetória artística.

A obra acompanha Fernanda Montenegro em trabalhos recentes no cinema e no teatro e, a partir dessas experiências, revisita o passado para mostrar como foi construída a carreira de uma das principais atrizes brasileiras.

Fernanda Montenegro estará em cartaz no Teatro Sesc Santos — Foto: Guilherme Pires/Divulgação

Pedro Waddington já dirigiu série sobre Anitta

Pedro Waddington acumula trabalhos no cinema, na televisão e no audiovisual. Entre seus projetos recentes estão a docussérie “Anitta: Made in Honório”, da Netflix, o especial de Natal “Gilda, Lúcia e o Bode”, exibido pela Globo, e episódios da série “Sob Pressão”.

Pedro também atuou como fotógrafo e codiretor de “Amor e Sorte: Gilda e Lúcia”, além de ter dirigido videoclipes de artistas como Ney Matogrosso e Gilberto Gil.

Seu filme “Precisamos Falar” também passou pelo Festival do Rio e pela Mostra de São Paulo, além de ter sido selecionado para o Festival de Biarritz 2025.

Produzido pela Conspiração em parceria com a NBCUniversal, o documentário sobre Fernanda Montenegro também conta com Andrucha Waddington, genro de Fernanda Montenegro, na produção.

A estreia de “Fernanda” no Festival do Rio marca a primeira exibição pública do longa.

articles.title: Boiadeirinha faz a festa da criançada no Festival de Inverno de Bonito | G1
articles.standfirst: Personagens inspirados no universo sertanejo levaram músicas, diversão e muita fofura ao festival na tarde desta sexta-feira (28).
articles.summary: Personagens inspirados no universo sertanejo levaram músicas, diversão e muita fofura ao festival na tarde desta sexta-feira (28)
articles.body:
Turma da Boiadeirinha alegra crianças no Festival de Inverno — Foto: Antonio Bispo

Enquanto a música sertaneja costuma reunir multidões nos grandes palcos, na tarde desta sexta-feira (28) foi a vez da criançada tomar conta do Festival de Inverno de Bonito .

A Turma da Boiadeirinha, personagem inspirada na cantora Ana Castela levou música, personagens e muita diversão para os pequenos que participaram do evento.

Os personagens também encantam a criança na televisão. A Turma da Boiadeirinha é o nome da série de animação infantil que aposta na música e na educação para criar um universo voltado às crianças.

Com músicas autorais e acompanhamento pedagógico, a produção trabalha valores como respeito, empatia e educação.

No festival, a atração também virou uma oportunidade para pais e filhos dividirem uma experiência juntos — e, para algumas famílias, foi a primeira vez em um evento desse tipo.

A cozinheira Elizete Rosa levou as filhas Soteles, de 5 anos, e outra criança de 10 anos para acompanhar o show.

Segundo ela, as meninas já conheciam a Turma da Boiadeirinha pela internet e são fãs das músicas. O encontro com os personagens no Festival de Inverno foi, portanto, uma experiência especial para a família.

“Ela é fã da banda, vê no YouTube”, contou Elizete.

Além da Turma da Boiadeirinha, as meninas também gostam de Ana Castela. Para elas, a programação infantil foi uma novidade.

“É a primeira vez que participa”, disse Elizete.

A família também aproveitou a estrutura preparada para receber as crianças no festival.

Crianças lotam show da Boiadeirinha — Foto: Antonio Bispo

A funcionária pública Edilaine Nunes Pereira também levou o filho para aproveitar a programação infantil. Para ela, acompanhar a empolgação da criança é parte da diversão.

“Eu sou super ‘cascalada’, eu gosto do que ele gosta, né? Eu fico empolgada para ele ver e ele está gostando”, contou.

Segundo Edilaine, o filho gosta de música e também se diverte cantando. A apresentação da Turma da Boiadeirinha foi a primeira experiência dele no festival.

A programação infantil ainda ganhou um significado especial para os pais: criar memórias ao lado dos filhos.

A proposta da Turma da Boiadeirinha é justamente aproximar gerações por meio da música e de experiências compartilhadas, criando momentos de troca entre pais e filhos, professores e alunos e também entre amigos.

No Festival de Inverno de Bonito, essa proposta saiu das telas e ganhou um palco, com direito a crianças cantando, famílias reunidas e muita animação.

Na noite desta sexta-feira (28) , quem sobe ao palco é o cantor Leo Foguete. O cantor mistura piseiro, forró e sertanejo, consolidando-se como uma das revelações da música nacional nas plataformas digitais.

No sábado (29) , Seu Jorge sobe ao palco. O cantor, compositor e ator mistura samba, soul, Música Popular Brasileira (MPB) e funk em um repertório com sucessos como "Burguesinha", "Mina do Condomínio" e "Amiga da Minha Mulher".

No domingo (30) , a dupla Humberto & Ronaldo encerra o festival. Os sertanejos trazem sucessos do sertanejo universitário para fechar o evento.

articles.title: Degnis Bofill: Vencedor do Grammy Latino é detido pelo ICE em Miami | G1
articles.standfirst: Degnis Nelson Bofill Miranda foi preso em 19 de agosto após desembarcar de um voo vindo de Nova York.
articles.summary: O percussionista Degnis Bofill, premiado no Grammy Latino, foi detido pelo ICE no aeroporto de Miami após retornar de compromissos profissionais em Nova York.
articles.body:
Degnis Nelson Bofill Miranda foi preso em 19 de agosto após desembarcar de um voo vindo de Nova York. — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

O percussionista e compositor cubano Degnis Bofill permanece sob custódia do serviço federal de imigração após ser detido por agentes do Serviço de Imigração e Alfândega (ICE) no Aeroporto Internacional de Miami, quando retornava de compromissos profissionais em Nova York.

Bofill, residente de Miami, foi detido em 19 de agosto após retornar de Nova York, onde havia participado da Latin Alternative Music Conference e se apresentado no Pocket Jazz Club, em Manhattan, segundo o “Miami New Times”.

A mulher do músico, Mara Delgado, afirmou que Bofill entrou nos Estados Unidos com um visto em 2023 e que seu pedido de asilo está pendente. Ela explicou que o caso ainda não havia chegado à fase de entrevista inicial quando ele foi detido.

“Estou preocupada com a possibilidade de ele ser deportado, porque não sei quando poderei vê-lo novamente”, disse Delgado à CBS News Miami.

Em comunicado à CBS News Miami, o ICE confirmou a prisão de Bofill e afirmou que ele entrou legalmente nos Estados Unidos em abril de 2023, mas posteriormente violou os termos de sua admissão no país. “Degnis Nelson Bofill Miranda, um imigrante cubano em situação irregular, foi preso pelo ICE em Miami em 19 de agosto durante uma operação de fiscalização migratória”, afirmou um porta-voz da agência.

Em 2022, Bofill venceu o Grammy Latino de Melhor Álbum Folclórico por “Ancestros Sinfónico”. Ao longo da carreira, excursionou por diversos países e se apresentou ao lado de artistas como Arturo O’Farrill, Orlando Valle “Maraca”, Néstor Torres, Bobby Carcassés, Dave Weckl, Blondie e Roberto Fonseca. Bofill também lidera seu próprio grupo, Golpes Libres, que mescla música tradicional afro-cubana e jazz contemporâneo.

articles.title: New movies to watch this weekend: See 'The Dog Stars' in theaters, rent 'Her Private Hell,' stream 'The Whisper Man' on Netflix
articles.summary: Jacob Elordi's new film was a miss for our critic — but the controversial "Coyote vs. Acme" is certainly worth a watch as it (finally!) hits theaters.
articles.body:
Welcome to Trust Me, I Watch Everything , a weekly guide to all the new movies out each Friday.

This week's biggest release is The Dog Stars, a Ridley Scott-directed, post-apocalyptic drama starring Jacob Elordi, Margaret Qualley, Josh Brolin and Guy Pearce. But the film with the most buzz has to be the hybrid live-action/animated movie Coyote vs. Acme , which almost didn't make it to screens at all.

If you'd rather stay home, you can now rent or buy Her Private Hell, the new film from Nicolas Winding Refn, or Motor City, an Alan Ritchson action vehicle.

Want to stick to a streaming service you're likely already paying for? The Whisper Man , with Adam Scott and Robert De Niro, debuts on Netflix, and Desert Warrior , the Saudi Arabian historical epic starring Anthony Mackie, makes its way to Hulu.

Why you should skip it: Ridley Scott's post-apocalyptic "thriller" — I put that in quotes for a reason — is not the action-heavy sci-fi flick that the trailers are selling. To put it simply, The Dog Stars is a shockingly derivative work that audiences have seen before, and there's just not enough variation or anything unique done with the subject matter here to recommend it.

Based on the 2012 book of the same name , The Dog Stars is set in a world ravaged by a pandemic. A widowed man (a brooding Jacob Elordi) lives a lonesome existence in a Colorado airplane hangar with his dog and a dour gunman he has befriended (Josh Brolin). When a mysterious transmission comes over the radio while he's flying his old Cessna, it sparks a hunt for the source of the sound.

It's every bit as generic as that sounds, and there unfortunately aren't any real surprises along the way. Despite admirable work from the cast, it never fully grabs you. It's so dull that I found my mind wandering to the question of why anybody would make this particular movie in 2026. There are obvious COVID parallels, but the film doesn't do anything with them. It feels dated and so familiar that it constantly begs the question: why?!

The biggest problem with it is that it lacks propulsiveness, or any sort of energy, really, until it's far too late. There's some action and excitement in the third act, which is well-staged in typical Ridley Scott fashion, though it feels at odds with the more grounded, melancholic, character-focused drama that makes up the rest of the film. The script is the biggest issue here, as the characters come off as archetypes more than real people. Scott is a strong enough director that his contributions, including some stunning aerial photography, do impress even when the rest is boring you to tears.

The Dog Stars does come to life at a certain point toward the end of its punishing 2-hour runtime — an uncanny sequence with Allison Janney has more verve than the rest of them combined — but the rest is as forgettable as movies get.

What other critics are saying : It's getting brutal reviews. TheWrap's William Bibbiani writes, "There are way too many faults in these Stars . Woof." Monica Castillo at the AV Club adds, "This messy look at the end of the world isn't Scott's darkest film, but it's one of his worst misfires."

How to watch : The Dog Stars is now playing in theaters nationwide.

Why I liked it: It's been three years since Warner Bros. decided that Coyote vs. Acme would be better for the company's bottom line if it were shelved indefinitely for a tax write-off rather than get a theatrical or even a streaming release.

Now, thanks to a smaller independent movie production company called Ketchup Entertainment — which also rescued another Looney Tunes movie that WB put on the chopping block, 2024's The Day the Earth Blew Up featuring Daffy Duck and Porky Pig — Coyote vs. Acme is triumphantly back from the dead.

The great irony of the entire ordeal, which led to tons of backlash for Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav and a groundswell of protests, online and in-person , demanding the movie be released, is that it's actually the best Looney Tunes movie ever made, by far.

The bar isn't exactly high; people my age likely have nostalgic affection for Space Jam, but it's not on the same level as Coyote vs. Acme, which feels more inspired by Who Framed Roger Rabbit? than other existing Looney Tunes hybrid live-action efforts.

After Acme products fail him one too many times in his dogged pursuit of the Roadrunner, Wile E. Coyote decides to hire a billboard lawyer (hilariously played by Saturday Night Live alum Will Forte) to sue the Acme Corporation, which is revealed to have nefarious motives for their faulty line of products. And perhaps Coyote has some secret motivations of his own for wanting to go to court.

The movie, already an underdog story, takes on a new resonance amid the drama with its release. It opens with text that jokes, "based on a true story," which makes you wonder whether they added that after all the WB turmoil. As film critic Matt Singer puts it, "I will leave it to you, dear reader, to decide why a studio in the midst of a massive merger with another studio would choose not to release a highly entertaining legal thriller about a cartoonishly evil mega-corporation engaged in conspiracies to maintain monopolistic control over the economy through their shady connections with a willfully ineffectual government."

The movie's integration of the cartoons into live action is easily the best in its field since Roger Rabbit . The cartoon violence is there to make the kids laugh, as effective a strategy as it ever was, and the adults get legal courtroom-drama gags cleverly modeled after Looney Tunes-esque mayhem.

The script from unlikely scribe Samy Burch, writer of the very adult Todd Haynes film May December , engages with the characters in a way I didn't expect and even found a bit moving. Using the Wile E. Coyote and Roadrunner cartoons to tell a story about dogged perseverance in the face of systemic oppressive forces conspiring against you sounds silly, and it absolutely is. The fact that it works so well onscreen is a testament to Burch's writing. And the entire debacle with its release strategy only makes its message that much more resonant.

Coyote vs. Acme is an unlikely and unexpected delight with a lot of heart, thankfully meeting the moment of its rallying cry against executive interference in art with its meta-commentary on corporate greed.

What other critics are saying: It's immediately beloved! Los Angeles Times' Amy Nicholson writes , "Wile E. Coyote isn't asking for a handout. If anything, he's a true believer in the American Dream, willingly and literally breaking his back to put food on his table." Tim Robey at the Telegraph writes, "While the novelty factor wears off after a while, what Dave Green's film gets bang on is reconsidering the eternal enmity between Coyote and Road Runner as a form of love story — a game of endless pursuit, catch me if you can."

How to watch: Coyote vs. Acme is now playing in theaters nationwide .

Buddy: Casper Kelly, the guy famous for the viral Too Many Cooks bizarro comedy sketch and the Adult Swim Yule Log comedy-horror movies, makes his leap into the mainstream with this uniquely weird horror movie about a killer children's TV show mascot . The premise is essentially, "what if a kid's show like Barney existed and Barney himself was an evil child murderer?" There are so many wild and fun ideas here, and the commitment to the bit is astounding, with incredible production design, costumes and invented characters. I appreciated how out-there and surreal it gets, and particularly loved the mascot-centric gore. Cristin Miloti and Topher Grace star, while Keegan-Michael Key voices the titular Buddy. Get tickets .

Colony: The director of the South Korean hit Train to Busan is back with a new zombie movie that does just enough new with the genre to make it feel exciting again. Trapped inside a sealed building during a deadly bioterrorist attack, a desperate group of survivors must navigate growing panic and betrayal as they fight to stay alive. The novel idea here is that the zombies are a hivemind, so when one zombie learns new information about how to attack its prey, all the zombies "update" with that new intel in real time. That twist, plus the idea of an evil villain controlling the zombies and starting the outbreak itself, gives it a freshness other zombie films lack. Colony also pays homage to genre classics, from George Romero to Resident Evil and The Last of Us, while charting its own path. It's a blast! Get tickets .

Idiots: The "off-putting-to-funny" ratio is off to a deadly degree in this alleged comedy starring Dave Franco, Mason Thames and O'Shea Jackson Jr. When two unqualified bozos are hired to transfer a rich teen to rehab, their straightforward gig quickly spirals into dangerous mayhem. It's too mean-spirited, the characters simply aren't much fun to be around and the plotting is increasingly hard to believe. On the other hand, it arguably has the funniest poop joke I've seen in a movie, though it's all downhill from there. Get tickets .

Why you should skip it: Nicolas Winding Refn, the filmmaker behind the Ryan Gosling cult hit Drive, returns from a 10-year hiatus from film with all of his cinematic obsessions still firmly in tow. This has a little bit of The Neon Demon, a lot of Only God Forgives and a setting that can best be compared to Blade Runner, if it were covered in a spooky layer of mist. That sentence makes about as much sense here as it does in the movie.

The synopsis is as follows: When a mysterious mist engulfs a futuristic metropolis, unleashing a deadly and elusive entity, a troubled young woman (Sophie Thatcher) searches for her father. Her quest collides with an American GI (Charles Melton) on a harrowing odyssey to rescue his daughter from Hell. Oh, and the entity is a giallo -style killer called The Leather Man, who literally rips women apart.

The film is nonlinear and incredibly abstract, and the dueling plots don't merge in a meaningful way; they just crudely coexist. Interviews with the filmmaker suggest the film is his response to becoming a dad, a girl dad specifically. Viewed through that lens, it's halfway interesting, but still feels more like a fetishistic object. Refn movies are brutally violent, usually at the expense of women, and Her Private Hell both reckons and indulges in that. If the story weren't so all over the place, he might've been onto something.

It's an astonishing movie to look at, though, with his trademark bisexual lighting deployed throughout. A beautiful, operatic score from long-retired Italian composer Pino Donaggio — his work Telescope, from Brian De Palma's Body Double, is among my favorite bits of movie music ever — is easily the highlight. It gives the film gravitas that it doesn't really deserve.

Her Private Hell is certainly the uncompromised vision of an auteur, but it reminded me that that's not always a good thing. In the same way that David Lynch movies are masterpieces rife with meaning to some and entirely incoherent to others, Her Private Hell is ambitious and has no interest in appealing to general audiences. It's a self-pastiche that will appeal only to existing fans of Refn and his eccentricities.

What other critics are saying: It's mostly been panned, but there are fans out there! Owen Gleiberman at Variety writes, "It's obvious that all of this coheres in Refn's mind, because he wouldn't have made it otherwise. But he has become seriously deluded about what an audience wants." The Guardian's Peter Bradshaw, however, dug it, writing that it "resists interpretation, like so many of Refn's recent films, but executes a slow dervish swirl of hypnotic strangeness."

How to watch: Her Private Hell is now available to rent or buy on Apple TV , Prime Video and other VOD platforms.

Why you should skip it: A compilation mixtape in search of a movie, Motor City is an almost entirely wordless action movie that assumes audiences will be happy with bare-minimum plotting as long as a song they enjoy is playing.

In 1970s Detroit, John Miller ( Alan Ritchson ) falls for a local gangster's girl and lands in prison for a crime he didn't commit. With his life ruined, Miller plots revenge against the man who took his girl away.

There's a moment early on in which the entirety of Fleetwood Mac's "The Chain," a 4-and-a-half-minute song, plays over a slow-motion action scene. It's so incredibly labored that the audience I saw it with was laughing at the movie, not with it.

Every scene is unnecessarily stretched out in similar ways, and you feel every second. It's gimmicky BS, frankly, that flattens the material into the most generic version of itself possible in an attempt to be different

What other critics are saying: Reviews are split. V ariety's Owen Gleiberman absolutely loved it , writing that it "qualifies as a true immersive cinematic experience. It's a movie almost entirely without words, but it speaks." The AV Club's Jesse Hassenger was more on my side, writing, "For movie-watchers who have wished that modern cinema was less reliant on boilerplate dialogue and tell-don't-show exposition dumps, Motor City plays like a monkey's paw curling in slow motion."

How to watch: Motor City is now available to rent or buy on Apple TV, Prime Video and other VOD platforms.

Hadestown: The Musical: This pro-shot version of the popular musical was filmed during a February 2025 London performance, reuniting the key Broadway cast members with West End performers. In the play, the tragic love of Orpheus and Eurydice is intertwined with the complex relationship of Hades and Persephone. Eurydice, living in poverty, is lured to the industrial underworld of Hadestown by Hades, while Orpheus, a struggling musician, ventures down below to bring her back. The selling point is the jaunty, fun, big-band New Orleans-y music throughout, alongside the lower-key folk tunes. The audience also plays a big part in the show, contributing to an atmosphere that feels more like a raucous party than a stuffy Broadway venue. But all those shots of the crowd having a blast do is remind the viewer that this movie version is limiting, and it would probably be more fun to see it in person. Rent or buy .

📺 Movies newly available on streaming services you may already have

Why you should skip it: At first glance, a throwback to the gritty '90s serial killer police procedurals à la Se7en with this starry cast looks and sounds great, but there's a reason you likely haven't heard a thing about it until it debuted unceremoniously on Netflix. It's a lifeless dud that, much like The Dog Stars reviewed above, feels too familiar and plays like a generic placeholder for something rather than a fully thought-out, fresh idea.

When his young son vanishes, a widower (Adam Scott) enlists help from his estranged father (Robert De Niro), a retired detective who put away the serial killer now linked to the case. Michelle Monaghan plays another detective.

Everybody is clearly phoning it in here, yet I still actually felt bad for the actors having to earnestly perform the uninspired clichés that make up the dialogue and exposition. Nobody's heart is in this, and it's clear from the opening scenes that "perfunctory" is the main register here. It's going-through-the-motions cinema at its snooziest.

If you want to watch a 2026 horror movie starring Adam Scott as an author with a missing and/or dead-person problem, check out Hokum instead.

What other critics are saying: Mary McNamara at the Los Angeles Times is much more forgiving, calling the film "as good as it gets" when it comes to streaming-only thrillers. "While it does not achieve the depth or brilliance of its obvious influences — The Silence of the Lambs, The Sixth Sense — it is a twisty and very welcome reminder of an age when psychological adrenaline-thumpers like Kiss the Girls and The Bone Collector drew crowds to the cineplex," she writes.

How to watch: The Whisper Man is now streaming on Netflix .

Why I liked it: When you think of 7th-century Arabia, surely your mind immediately goes to Anthony Mackie and Sharlto Copley, right?

If you're able to put aside the inherent absurdity of the casting, Desert Warrior is actually far more competent than it sounds on paper, mostly thanks to esteemed director Rupert Wyatt ( Rise of the Planet of the Apes) , who imbues the action with life and fills the movie with gorgeous desert images.

It's a $150 million Saudi-backed film, and the money is, in fact, on the screen. The poster and title may lead you to believe that Mackie is the titular desert warrior, but the movie is smarter than that and has a real plot that actually makes sense.

In the film, Princess Hind (Aiysha Hart, the real desert warrior here) defies her fate, refusing to become a concubine to the ruthless Emperor Kisra (Sir Ben Kingsley). Fleeing into the desert with her father, she is hunted by a merciless army and forced to trust a legendary bandit (Mackie) who has secrets of his own. Rising from fugitive to fearless warrior, Hind unites warring tribes for a final battle that will change history forever.

Desert Warrior makes the absolute most of on-location filming in exotic locales; it's beautifully photographed throughout, and the set pieces are all exciting and well put together. Surely many liberties have been taken in adapting this slice of history into an action film, but in the process, Saudi Arabia proves it can make a big-budget spectacle that largely stands up to the best Hollywood has to offer, largely because Hollywood doesn't even try to make historical epics anymore.

What other critics are saying: They were not as kind as myself. The AV Club's Monica Castillo writes, "While the story onscreen is dull and the performances uninspired, it's the story around Desert Warrior that solidifies it as a strange chapter in a country's self-promotional history."

How to watch: Desert Warrior is now streaming on Hulu .

Penny Lane is Dead: This Aussie gem set in 1986 follows three best friends' celebration at a beach house that turns into a blood-soaked fight for survival when a prank goes horribly wrong. It's an Evil Cousin horror flick, which should become its own genre, I've decided. Australian cinema can be a particularly cruel and unrelenting breed, and this movie certainly fits that bill. It's got a lot on its mind, from toxic masculinity to internalized misogyny, and also stages some nasty violence, but in a way that doesn't revel in it. The movie is just as sickened by the proceedings as you are. Now streaming on Shudder. That's all for this week! We'll see you next Friday.

articles.title: Six people injured after sign falls at Christian festival near Steyning
articles.summary: Emergency services were called to reports of people in need of medical attention at Wiston Park.
articles.body:
Six people have been injured by a falling sign at a Christian festival in West Sussex.

Emergency services were called to reports of multiple people in need of medical attention at Big Church Festival, near Steyning, shortly after 15:30 BST on Friday.

Ambulance crews, critical care paramedics and specialist response teams are at the scene, according to South East Coast Ambulance Service.

Organisers said that the event had been "paused" following a "serious incident" and that no further programming would take place on Friday.

"First and foremost, our thoughts and prayers are with those who have been directly impacted by the incident," the organisers added.

"We understand this will be deeply disappointing for the thousands who have joined us at the festival."

Andrew Griffith, MP for Arundel and South Downs, said: "Concerned to hear reports of casualties at the Big Church festival at Wiston.

"There have certainly been strong gusts of wind during the course of this afternoon locally.

"My thoughts are with all of those impacted at this time and those responding to the incident."

The festival said that it was working closely with emergency services and the authorities, with further announcements to be made as more information becomes available.

"We are grateful for the understanding, patience, and prayers of our community at this time," it added.

Organisers earlier wrote on social media that "all day visitors must leave the site now."

"If you are camping with us, please return to your campsite and await further updates," they added.

Campers were also able to leave the site if they wished to do so.

Traffic disruption is expected in the area, and the public are urged to seek alternative routes, Sussex Police said.

Officers said they were called to the site off Washington Road at about 15:40 and remained at the scene.

The Big Church Festival - which describes itself as the UK's biggest Christian festival - was founded in 2009.

This year's sold-out edition of the event started on Friday and was set to run until Sunday.

articles.title: Tennessee intends to name Nashville airport after Dolly Parton, Governor says
articles.summary: By Daphne Psaledakis WASHINGTON, Aug 28 (Reuters) - Tennessee intends to name Nashville International Airport after country music icon Dolly Parton, accordin...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, Aug 28 (Reuters) - Tennessee intends to name Nashville International Airport after country music icon Dolly Parton, according to ‌a statement on Friday, after the singer died in the country ‌music capital at age 80 earlier this week.

The decision comes after a social media campaign ​by fans to change the airport's name to honor Parton after her death. Tennessee Governor Bill Lee spoke with Parton's team about the move this week, according to statements from the airport and Lee's office.

"Dolly Parton's extraordinary ‌life is forever woven into ⁠the fabric of our state," Lee said in the statement.

"At a place where Tennessee welcomes the world, it is ⁠fitting that Nashville International Airport would bear the name of our state's favorite daughter and greet travelers with the enduring legacy of Dolly's music, generosity, faith, ​and ​kindness."

The proposal to rename the airport and ​the current Metro Nashville Airport ‌Authority's naming policy will be addressed at a meeting on September 17, according to the statement. The current policy prohibits naming any property after a person who has not been dead for at least two years, The New York Times reported.

Parton was born on January 19, 1946, in Pittman ‌Center, Tennessee, and grew up in a ​one-room cabin in nearby Locust Ridge.

She was ​appearing on the Grand Ole ​Opry, a weekly country music concert in Nashville, Tennessee, ‌at age 13, and after graduating ​from high school, she ​moved to Nashville to pursue a music career.

With classic songs including "Coat of Many Colors," "Jolene" and "I Will Always Love You," Parton became one ​of the best-selling female ‌artists of all time, with over 100 million records sold. ​She won 11 Grammy Awards, including a Lifetime Achievement Award.

(Reporting by ​Daphne Psaledakis; Editing by Caitlin Webber)

articles.title: Former Disney Channel star alleges she was sexually abused at 14 after being told to ‘bond’ with employee
articles.summary: Raquel Lee Bolleau alleges an adult employee sexually abused her when she was 14 on a Disney Channel set after personnel encouraged her to "bond" with him.
articles.body: A former Disney Channel star made disturbing allegations about her time on set in a new lawsuit. Raquel Lee Bolleau claimed an adult male employee sexually abused her when she was just 14 after Disney personnel allegedly encouraged her to "bond" with him. The alleged abuse began during production of the 2001 Disney Channel movie "The Poof Point," after personnel directed her to spend time with the adult employee. FORMER DISNEY STAR MAITLAND WARD SAYS YOUNG ACTORS WERE TREATED LIKE A 'PRODUCT' IN HOLLYWOOD FACTORY According to the complaint obtained by Fox News Digital, the man supplied the 14-year-old with alcohol and repeatedly sexually assaulted her during filming. After the alleged sexual assault, Bolleau recalled the employee telling her, "You're old enough. You can handle it." Bolleau claimed she returned to set smelling of alcohol, vomiting and visibly changed after the alleged assault, but Disney personnel failed to investigate how a 14-year-old got alcohol or seek medical care for her. Instead, the complaint claimed, an executive branded her "out of control," said the movie had gone "haywire" and told her representatives Disney was "extremely upset." On another occasion, an on-set Disney executive producer allegedly repeatedly told Bolleau she "need[ed] Jesus" and told her mother, "your daughter has a demon inside her," according to the complaint. Bolleau alleged Disney repeatedly separated her from her guardian despite California protections requiring a guardian of a performer under 16 remain within "sight or sound" of the child. According to the complaint, her guardian could not watch Bolleau while she filmed or accompany her to wardrobe and makeup, and production personnel once told the guardian, "We do not even need you on set." Bolleau claimed those practices left her without adequate adult supervision and gave her alleged abuser unrestricted access to her. 'LITTLE HOUSE ON THE PRAIRIE' STAR SAYS CHILD ACTORS GET 'DROPPED' AFTER HOLLYWOOD FAME FADES Bolleau alleged the employee also sexually harassed and touched her in front of others on set. She claimed he regularly gave her unsolicited hugs, rubbed his genitals against her and whispered comments including "last night was so good" while cast members were still wearing microphones. Bolleau alleged sound technicians could hear many of the comments, but no one intervened or asked what the adult employee was saying to her. "Instead of protecting and supporting its minor employee who was being repeatedly raped, sexually assaulted, sexually abused, and harassed, Disney covered up Mr. Doe’s abuse, and blamed Ms. Bolleau for the impact of Mr. Doe’s horrific misconduct," Bolleau's lawyers wrote. "Disney’s egregious role in Mr. Doe’s abuse of Ms. Bolleau is part of a broader, institutional, and systemic pattern of institutional and individual failures at Disney that extends far beyond 'The Poof Point.'" Bolleau claimed the alleged abuse continued after filming wrapped. According to the complaint, Disney booked Bolleau in first class while seating her guardian in economy on the flight back to California. Bolleau alleged the employee told her to sit next to him and bring a blanket to cover them before sexually assaulting her during the flight and continuing until their row began to deboard at Los Angeles International Airport. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Bolleau sued The Walt Disney Company, specifically alleging Disney failed to protect her from sexual abuse when she was a 14-year-old actress. She claimed the company ignored warning signs, violated child-actor protections and failed to properly supervise her alleged abuser. She is seeking compensatory and punitive damages, along with attorneys’ fees, costs and interest. "Over the last decade, countless child actors have come forward to bravely share their experiences of abuse by adults in entertainment," Bolleau's lawyers, Doug Wigdor and Jane Kim, told Fox News Digital in a statement. "As former government prosecutors, our message to the entertainment industry is simple: This conduct is inexcusable, and those involved – directly or indirectly – must be held accountable." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Bolleau began acting as a child, with an early television appearance on "Malcolm & Eddie" before getting her breakout opportunity on Nickelodeon’s "The Amanda Show." She appeared as a regular performer during the sketch comedy series’ first season alongside Amanda Bynes. She subsequently moved into Disney projects, playing Marie, the sister of Tahj Mowry’s Eddie, in "The Poof Point." Bolleau claimed Disney threatened and did cancel her role in a production after the alleged sexual assault in 2001 in the lawsuit. Disney did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. articles.title: Demi Lovato celebrates 34th birthday in colorful string bikini during Bahamas getaway
articles.summary: Demi Lovato shared jet ski photos in a colorful bikini during her Bahamas birthday getaway, days after turning 34 and celebrating a milestone year.
articles.body: Demi Lovato is keeping her birthday celebration going in the Bahamas. The 34-year-old singer kept the birthday fun going Thursday, sharing new shots of herself riding a jet ski in a colorful bikini against the bright blue Bahamas water. Lovato opened the Instagram carousel with a close-up selfie taken while sitting on a red jet ski. JESSICA SIMPSON TURNS HEADS IN BIKINI PHOTOS FROM TRIP TO TURKS AND CAICOS She wore a red, black and yellow patterned string bikini with dark sunglasses and small hoop earrings. Her dark hair fell loosely around her shoulders as she leaned toward the camera for the selfie. "Hi," Lovato captioned the post. "Bye!" she added. A second photo showed the singer from farther away on the same jet ski, giving a wider look at the colorful swimsuit and surrounding water. Fans quickly flooded the comments with praise for Lovato's vacation photos. One fan referenced Lovato’s 2015 hit, writing, "She’s really cool for the summer." "You’re prettier than the prettiest water I’ve ever seen!" another added. One commenter also pointed out how the look coordinated with the jet ski, writing, "The suit matching the jet ski 🙂‍↕️" PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE The new photos came just days after Lovato shared more highlights from the same Bahamas getaway. "Someone’s gotta hold it down in the bahamas," she captioned the earlier post. BRITTANY ALDEAN WOWS IN VACATION STYLE DURING BAHAMAS GETAWAY WITH JASON ALDEAN In one of those photos, Lovato stood in shallow water wearing a bright red string bikini with both arms raised above her head. She smiled as the clear water surrounded her, while the tropical shoreline could be seen in the distance. SOFIA VERGARA SIZZLES IN RED BIKINI WHILE CELEBRATING 54TH BIRTHDAY ON YACHT IN ITALY Another image captured Lovato floating on her back in the water in the same red bikini. The singer stretched out across the surface with her arms relaxed at her sides as the blue water filled the frame. Lovato turned 34 on Aug. 20. The birthday getaway comes during a celebratory year for the singer, who recently marked her first wedding anniversary with husband Jordan "Jutes" Lutes. Lovato and Lutes married in California in May 2025 after first going public with their relationship in 2022. Earlier this month, Lovato opened up about what she has learned during her first year of marriage. "When you’re able to communicate with each other what you need, what you want, it creates a safe space for the two of you to share your feelings with one another," Lovato told People at the Aug. 10 premiere of "Camp Rock 3." So I think communication is a big part of that," she added. The singer also recently returned to one of the roles that helped launch her career. Lovato reprised her role as Mitchie Torres in "Camp Rock 3" and served as an executive producer on the film alongside the Jonas Brothers. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? Lovato's Disney roots stretch back to her childhood, when she appeared on "Barney & Friends." She later broke out as Mitchie Torres in "Camp Rock" before starring in her own Disney Channel series, "Sonny with a Chance." articles.title: 'Veronica Mars' star Jason Dohring traded Hollywood for farming
articles.summary: Jason Dohring told his agents he was going to farm, and now the "Veronica Mars" star runs an 11-acre regenerative farm in Florida with his family.
articles.body: "Veronica Mars" star Jason Dohring has stepped away from acting to focus on a new passion. During a recent appearance on the "Don't Do Nothing" podcast, the 44-year-old actor shared that he developed an interest in gardening around four years ago and told his agents, "I'm just going to go farm for a minute." "I just got an interest in it and I've kind of the last three years I built like, I'm on my third farm now and we're just making great food for people cause I really realized that people are getting sick from the food that they're eating," he said. He first began planting in Los Angeles, before developing a 14-acre farm in West Virginia, where they planted 4,000 trees, including apples, cherries, pears, peaches and nectarines, noting he probably planted "3,500 of them myself." 'THE THORN BIRDS' STAR RACHEL WARD TRADED 'EMPTY' HOLLYWOOD FOR FARM LIFE IN AUSTRALIA The actor now lives on an 11-acre farm in Florida with his wife, Lauren Kutner, and their four kids, noting he moved there because of the weather. He said that when farming in California, they weren't allowed to drill a well and would run out of water. "L.A. is crazy. [You can go] eight, nine months with no rain. You know what I mean?" he said. "That's when I when we moved to Florida I was like we get infinite rain. We have infinite manure. Like you know you could farm for free." Dohring is proud of his Florida farm and the regenerative farming method he uses, which involves growing the crops without chemicals. Through this method, he says that on his farm, "stuff is starting to get much better." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "There was this old guy and he's like, ‘Are you the owner?’" he said about a recent experience on his farm. "And he's like, ‘I've been praying to God that the gate was open so I could come in here and see this cause I've been in agriculture since I was 12. I've never seen anything like this before.’" Dohring first rose to fame playing Logan Echolls on "Veronica Mars" opposite Kristen Bell, for three seasons, from 2004 to 2007. He starred in several other projects, including "Moonlight" and "The Originals," before returning to film the "Veronica Mars" feature movie in 2014 and the one-season revival in 2019. His last acting gig was four episodes of "SEAL Team" in 2021. While he has stepped away from acting for now, he admits, "I'll probably jump back into it at some point," adding he has already done a short film for a friend. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE "I love art, and when I get around art, even talking about this is exciting to me," he said. "I think there's something in everybody that is aesthetic, meaning beautiful or wants to create." The actor married Kutner in 2004, shortly before "Veronica Mars" premiered. The two first met and became friends while in high school, with Dohring saying their friendship is the foundation of their marriage. Since getting married, the couple have welcomed four children: son Owen, and daughters Lily, Ainsley Mae and Isla Avery. "My wife and I were married 20 years ago today," he wrote on Instagram in July 2024. "We have had an amazing life together, including raising four incredible children. I consider her my best friend." articles.title: Charli XCX electrifies Reading Festival with era-spanning set
articles.summary: The British singer and Irish rock band Fontaines DC both headlined the first night of Reading for 2026.
articles.body:
Charli XCX has ushered in her next era with an electrifying headline set at Reading Festival which showcased hits from across her music career.

It marked the British singer's first UK festival performance since releasing her latest studio album - Music, Fashion, Film - which is a pivot from her culture-shaping, electronic-pop record Brat and features more of a rock edge.

But her Friday evening show highlighted the best of both, alongside fan favourite tracks from her back catalogue.

She also upped the production from her last Brat tour, with more elaborate staging, numerous costume changes, dramatic pyro and strobe lighting, and she was accompanied by a host of dancers and a live band.

Distorted, black-and-white videos of Charli kicked off the performance and the tens of thousands who had gathered at the main stage erupted as the chords were struck up to her new album's lead single, Rock Music.

After delivering punchy renditions of new tracks Wink Wink, Yeah and Card Declined, she stepped out to change from a black sparkly blazer into a black corseted dress.

The second act of the performance showcased the breadth of her work, as she moved from pop hit Track 10 from her 2017 mixtape, to the melancholic tones of House, which she co-wrote for the recent Wuthering Heights soundtrack album.

Those still craving her infectious dance tracks welcomed the singer later breaking out songs like Club Classics, 365 and the Grammy-winning Von Dutch from her sixth album Brat, which became a cultural phenomenon and propelled her to new heights in 2024.

After returning to the more punk style of Music, Fashion, Film, she closed with its last track, No One Lasts Forever.

The song concludes with filmmaker David Cronenberg saying "no one lasts forever / they are dead, they are gone" and "oblivion is freedom" - and Charli let that be the last words which rang out as she stared out across the crowd, surrounded by her dancers.

The rock energy continued on the main stage as Fontaines DC followed Charli, with both acts billed as headliners for the opening night of Reading.

Fans had to wait about half an hour longer due to a delay, but the Irish rock band from Dublin soon won them back around as they launched into hits like Favourite and I Love You.

They closed out the set with their Grammy-nominated track Starbuster from their fourth album, Romance, with the crowd responding by chanting the lyrics back to them.

Ahead of Charli's set, grime artist Skepta also channelled some Brat energy when he took to the main stage in a lime green waterproof jacket as he powered through the downpours to hype up the crowd.

The rapper belting out "it rains, it pours" from his hit collaboration track, Praise the Lord (Da Shine), with A$AP Rocky was particularly fitting, and he ended the set on a high as the crowd jumped along to Victory Lap, his collaboration with Fred Again.. and PlaqueBoyMax.

The rainstorms drew more festival-goers into the new Gallery tent, but US rock band Geese had already pulled in a huge crowd who jumped and head-banged along to guitar-heavy tracks like Half Real and 100 Horses.

Earlier in the afternoon, BBC Radio 1's Sound of 2026 winner Skye Newman's powerful, husky vocals reverberated through the same tent as she performed hit songs like FU & UF and Family Matters.

Jamie T kicked off the main stage at midday after posting a video the day before asking if he could get a "last minute" set, and he used his 33 minutes and 10 seconds, a nod to his new single 3310, to crack out some of his indie hits, including Zombie and Sticks N Stones.

The twin festivals will feature six major headliners this weekend, with bosses previously saying Reading and Leeds will be the only UK festival appearances for all of them this year.

Rapper Dave, singer-songwriter Raye, electronic duo Chase & Status and band Florence + The Machine are all set to top the bill.

articles.title: Tennessee moves to rename Nashville airport for Dolly Parton days after beloved icon's death
articles.summary: Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee announced plans to rename Nashville International Airport after Dolly Parton following a petition with over 155,000 signatures.
articles.body: Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee and Nashville International Airport announced Friday that they intend to name the airport in honor of Dolly Parton, moving toward a major tribute to the icon after an outpouring of public support for the beloved late country music legend's legacy. Lee said he spoke with Parton's team about the proposal this week. Her team expressed appreciation for the support and is open to continuing the conversation, according to a joint announcement from the governor and the Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority. The proposal would place Parton's name on the gateway to Music City, connecting the transportation hub with a woman whose music, philanthropy and deeply rooted connection to her home state made her perhaps its most celebrated figure. TRUMP MOURNS DOLLY PARTON, ORDERS US FLAGS LOWERED NATIONWIDE AFTER COUNTRY MUSIC ICON DIES "Dolly Parton’s extraordinary life is forever woven into the fabric of our state," said Lee about the Tennessee native, who died Tuesday at 80 after a brief cancer battle. "From her rural mountain home in East Tennessee to global stages, Dolly carried the Volunteer Spirit with her. "At a place where Tennessee welcomes the world, it is fitting that Nashville International Airport would bear the name of our state’s favorite daughter and greet travelers with the enduring legacy of Dolly’s music, generosity, faith, and kindness." The announcement comes amid a groundswell of support for renaming the airport after Parton. A Change.org petition titled "Rename Nashville International Airport to Dolly Parton International Airport" had accumulated 155,501 verified signatures, according to the petition page. DOLLY PARTON DEFIED COUNTRY MUSIC'S EXPECTATIONS FOR WOMEN AND BUILT A CAREER ON HER OWN TERMS: EXPERTS The petition was originally launched in January 2025 by Lydia Popovich and Dan Dion, who argued that Parton's influence extended far beyond the music that made her famous, pointing to her philanthropy and her Imagination Library literacy program. Following Parton's death this week, the organizers said tens of thousands of additional supporters signed the petition and renewed their effort to have Nashville's airport carry her name. The campaign has also drawn support from Tennessee officials. State Rep. Todd Warner said in a response published on the petition page that he would introduce legislation supporting the change. "Yes I will definitely introduce legislation to rename the BNA airport Dolly Parton International Airport! Thanks, TW," Warner wrote, according to the response reproduced by Change.org. DOLLY PARTON'S LIFE IN HER OWN WORDS: FROM SMOKY MOUNTAINS POVERTY TO COUNTRY MUSIC IMMORTALITY Nashville Council member Russ Bradford also said he would sponsor a resolution asking the Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority to consider the change, while stressing that the authority, rather than the council, has the ultimate say over the airport's name. "I'm proud to sponsor a resolution asking the Metro Nashville Airport Authority to consider renaming BNA to Dolly Parton International Airport," Bradford said in a response published by Change.org. The tribute carries particular resonance because Parton had previously resisted efforts to put her own legacy on a pedestal. In 2021, Parton asked Tennessee lawmakers to withdraw a bill that would have allowed a statue of her to be erected on the grounds of the state Capitol. STEVE DOOCY: THE DOLLY PARTON I SAW WHEN THE CAMERAS STOPPED ROLLING "I am honored and humbled by their intention, but I have asked the leaders of the state legislature to remove the bill from any and all consideration," Parton said at the time in a post shared to social media. She explained that she did not believe such an honor was appropriate while the country was confronting larger challenges, but left open the possibility that Tennessee might honor her in that way someday. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Given all that is going on in the world, I don't think putting me on a pedestal is appropriate at this time," Parton said. "I hope, though, that somewhere down the road several years from now or perhaps after I'm gone if you still feel I deserve it, then I'm certain I will stand proud in our great State Capitol as a grateful Tennessean." The proposal to rename the airport will be discussed at the Metro Nashville Airport Authority’s next meeting on Sept. 17, according to their release.

articles.title: 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-ups' box office collection day 3: Yash-Nayanthara starrer sees 29.3 percent decline; mints Rs 23.75 crore overseas
articles.summary: Yash and Nayanthara's 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-ups' continued its theatrical run on Friday. The movie recorded a drop in its domestic earnings o.
articles.body: Yash and Nayanthara's 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-ups' continued its theatrical run on Friday. The movie recorded a drop in its domestic earnings on Day 3. However, it managed to take its India net collection beyond the Rs 150 crore mark within three days.Toxic Movie ReviewAccording to Sacnilk day 3 report, 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-ups' has earned Rs 165.35 crore net in India so far, with its total domestic gross collection standing at Rs 197.70 crore. The movie has also grossed Rs 23.75 crore overseas, taking its worldwide gross collection to Rs 221.45 crore.'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-ups' collected an estimated Rs 26.60 crore net in India on its third day. The movie had earned Rs 37.65 crore on Day 2. Its latest figure represents a 29.3% decline from Thursday's collection.The Geetu Mohandas directorial has now collected Rs 165.35 crore net in India. Its total India gross collection stands at Rs 197.70 crore.'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-ups' Day 3 box office collection'Toxic' opened with an estimated Rs 101.10 crore net on Wednesday. The movie then collected Rs 37.65 crore on Thursday. Its Day 3 earnings stood at Rs 26.60 crore.The movie recorded 25.5% overall occupancy on Friday. It was screened across 19,390 shows in India. Despite the decline in daily earnings, the three-day total has remained strong.Day 1: Rs 101.10 croreDay 2: Rs 37.65 croreDay 3: Rs 26.60 croreThe movie's cumulative India net collection is now Rs 165.35 crore.Language-wise collection of 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-ups'The Hindi version remained the biggest contributor to the movie's Day 3 earnings. It collected an estimated Rs 19.15 crore. The Kannada version added Rs 5 crore to the total.The Telugu version earned approximately Rs 1.50 crore. The Tamil version contributed Rs 75 lakhs. The Malayalam version recorded Rs 20 lakhs.The Hindi version registered 26.75% overall occupancy. Its night shows recorded the highest occupancy at 39.62%. The Kannada version performed better, with 36.12% overall occupancy. Its night shows reached 50.31%. The Telugu version recorded 18.21% overall occupancy. Tamil registered 20.83% overall occupancy.'Toxic' worldwide box office collectionAccording to the reported figures, 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-ups' collected Rs 4 crore overseas on day 3.Its cumulative overseas gross collection has reached Rs 23.75 crore. The movie's worldwide gross collection now stands at Rs 221.45 crore.What did ETimes say about 'Toxic'?ETimes awarded 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-ups' three stars out of five. The review praised the movie's style and violence.The review read, "Toxic has style and violence in abundance, but substance in short supply. The screenplay is uneven, the runtime feels excessive, several characters are underdeveloped, and the emotional beats do not always hit home. Beneath the guns, bloodshed, machismo and spectacle is a potentially compelling story about abandonment, inherited trauma, masculine violence and the complicated relationship between fathers and sons. The film clearly knows what it wants to say. It just doesn’t always know how to make us feel it."DISCLAIMER: The box office numbers and the data in this article are compiled from public and industry sources. All figures are approximate unless explicitly mentioned, offering a fair representation of the movie's box office performance. These totals may change as official studio data is updated or as additional international market reports are finalized.
